applies_where: Licking County screen (~3.03 mi), in Jersey/Plain township boundary contexts and New Albany municipal portions; actual controlling roads to be proven station-by-station.
route_station_reference: S0 early features per route_station_ahj_candidate_register.csv; S0-S001 etc. ODOT D5 is not candidate state owner within current state-route screen.
permit_trigger_and_submission: County road utility ROW permit; township/city permit separately if their road/ROW. County utility form requires 2 plan copies, plan references to pavement, ROW, property lines, cross-section for crossing under pavement and drainage structures.
existing_utilities_plan_rule: Required drawings show pavement, ROW, property and drainage; existing utility plotting not expressly specified in instructions reviewed. Include all located known utilities for review and safety.
published_review_clock: No utility permit review SLA found.
fees_and_bonds: Public page links current ROW utility application; fee not found on reviewed page. Confirm fee, insurance/bond, separate/blanket permit.
design_or_construction_constraints: No pavement cuts; 36 in minimum cable depth below pavement, ditch/channel and around cross culverts/bridges; call Highway Dept 24h before work; traffic per OMUTCD; restore topsoil/sod. Current approved/sample permits state no county ROW work Dec1-Apr15 absent Engineer exception and completion by Dec1.
schedule_risk: Season closes the window Dec1-Apr15 unless written exception; route schedule/permit completion must fit. Clarify with Licking for current standard application.
source_status: Current county application instructions plus sample issued permits; season-specific wording should be confirmed on permit form.

applies_where: Franklin County screen (~20.12 mi), including city/place and township boundary overlays; actual roads split by owner/controller.
route_station_reference: S0/S1 feature intervals in route_station_ahj_candidate_register.csv. State route candidates at multiple station ranges in ODOT District 6 file.
permit_trigger_and_submission: Written utility road-ROW authorization for County-controlled roads; township/municipal ROW approvals are separate if their road. County application asks along/across and named road/township; attach plans.
existing_utilities_plan_rule: County application located does not provide clear full utility drawing checklist. Show known utilities, drainage, plan/profile, work zone, ROW and restoration to make routing reviewable; request county checklist.
published_review_clock: No reliable county Engineer utility-review SLA found; do not reuse 3-week Franklin County EDP development-review notice.
fees_and_bonds: Current fee/bond schedule for utility ROW not established in official materials reviewed; ask County Engineer.
design_or_construction_constraints: Permit holder restores pavement/shoulder/drainage; maintains traffic, indemnifies County; surfaced older county permit expires 30d after issue and requires call before start, but current applicability must be confirmed. Franklin County Drainage District permit may also be triggered by crossing facilities; district applications have published $150 minimum fee and $10,000 prepaid inspection per facility crossing under its 2025 form. Verify whether this route intersects a district before relying on that amount.
schedule_risk: County road vs township vs Columbus/Worthington/New Albany/Powell permit, drainage district crossings, separate D6 state highway approvals, ROW evidence.
source_status: Authority/conditions depend on actual road; old permit form not treated as current SLA.

authority_or_permit_track: Delaware County Engineer / Concord, Liberty or Genoa Township / City
applies_where: Delaware County screen (~16.81 mi); Concord/Liberty/Orange/other township boundary overlays and Powell/New Albany/Columbus places. Delaware County Engineer handles county roads and townships except named township self-issuers; route-specific road proof required.
route_station_reference: S0/S1 feature intervals in route_station_ahj_candidate_register.csv; D6 candidate state roads S1-S029, S1-S032, S1-S034 etc.
permit_trigger_and_submission: Public utility permit for County-controlled county/township road ROW; submit 4-8 weeks before start. City streets to cities; state highways to ODOT. Concord/Liberty self-issue ROW; Genoa includes ROW per current County permit page.
existing_utilities_plan_rule: Checklist explicitly requires existing pavement and ROW with dimensions, proposed work dimensions from pavement edge, utility size/length, station references; instructions found do not explicitly require every existing utility to be plotted. Show all located existing utilities and drainage anyway.
published_review_clock: 4-8 week submission window, not processing-duration SLA. ROW work form says 7 working days, but do not substitute that for utility application window.
fees_and_bonds: Current permit page says utility NO fee; inspection fee may be assessed when necessary; verify insurance and route-specific inspection costs.
design_or_construction_constraints: No work within 5 ft of edge of pavement; 48 in cover at all road crossings; hard-surface roads bored unless cut approved; 100% inspector employed by applicant; traffic/restoration by applicant; notify county 2 working days before work; permit valid one year.
schedule_risk: File 4-8 weeks ahead or miss allowable window; 48-in profile impacts bore feasibility and water/utility conflicts; 5-ft setback may push route into private property/ROW line; separate self-issuing township/city D6 permits.
source_status: County Public Utility Permit Process and utility form, current online fee page.

applies_where: Union County screen (~11.30 mi), Marysville city overlay plus candidate county/township road segments. State routes US23/US36/US33 have D6 candidates near S1-S028 and S1-S042–044.
route_station_reference: S1 later features in route_station_ahj_candidate_register.csv; route station state candidates in ohio_state_route_station_summary.csv.
permit_trigger_and_submission: Permit for all county road ROW work before work; separate permit for each non-contiguous work segment unless blanket permit granted at Engineer discretion. Submit in duplicate and include construction plans. City streets and actual state ROW separately.
existing_utilities_plan_rule: YES: published plans expressly show existing utilities, centerline, ROW, edge of pavement, bridge/culvert, drainage, swales, catch basins, manholes, fences and structures; proposed work size/depth/details and profile/elevation as required.
published_review_clock: Generally approved within 2 working days, and submissions generally not less than 3 business days prior to start; target assumes complete acceptable package, not a statutory entitlement.
fees_and_bonds: No fee schedule found in reviewed requirements; confirm current fees.
design_or_construction_constraints: Minimum cover 3 ft under pavement, 2.5 ft under sod ditches, 2 ft under paved ditches/other surfaces. For <=16-in fiber conduit crossings under HMA, use method other than open cut approved by Engineer. Maintain traffic; closure needs Commissioner permission; notify Sheriff/fire 2 days ahead; Engineer notified 2 days prestart and at restoration/stoppage/resumption; 120-day permit life.
schedule_risk: HMA crossings, river/bridge conditions, permit segmentation, and municipal vs county road jurisdiction.
source_status: Published Union County ROW requirements, effective base text 1999 and current posted PDF; confirm any superseding resolution/fee.

authority_or_permit_track: City of Columbus Public Service / 903 ROW Excavation
applies_where: Municipality boundary overlay ~15.23 mi; exact roadway ownership/ROW must be verified. Intersects candidate ODOT routes and City reservoir parcels, which are distinct control/ownership tracks.
route_station_reference: Municipality route spans in station_ahj_boundary_intervals.csv; candidate route feature windows in route_station_ahj_candidate_register.csv / ohio_state_route_station_summary.csv.
permit_trigger_and_submission: 903 excavation permit for excavation in City public street/sidewalk/grass strip, including placement/maintenance of underground telecom facilities. City online portal. 903 plan routing review by City departments.
existing_utilities_plan_rule: Plan checklist demands plan/profile, bore pits, route station breaks, offsets, method, perpendicular crossings and minimum 3-ft horizontal / 1-ft vertical clearance statement from existing utilities; show utilities sufficient to demonstrate compliance. OUPS note required.
published_review_clock: No 903 excavation/utility SLA found. Separate 906 occupancy permit clock: file 5 business days ahead (10 full lane closure); decision in 5 days plus written extension 5 days. 906 is not the permanent utility-excavation clock.
fees_and_bonds: 2026 903 fee details are online in portal/application attachment; no amount transcribed here. Confirm current application-specific permit, inspection, patch/repair, MOT, bond and insurance fees.
design_or_construction_constraints: 3-year moratorium on cut into new/re-paved street (emergency leaks exception); 5-year Special Improved Street moratorium; joint use existing facilities if adequate capacity; pedestrian 6ft clearance for sidewalk occupancy; city department requirements may add tree/forestry/drainage/traffic review.
schedule_risk: CIP street repaving/special streets; City utility crossing clearance; multiple-review department routing; traffic closure and restoration; ODOT/bridge concurrency if crossing state facility.
source_status: Current 903 rules and checklist; municipal polygon does not prove city owns every road.

existing_utilities_plan_rule: Local checklist not yet verified for each municipality/township; submit existing utility inventory, profiles, pits, ROW and crossings as baseline, then confirm authority-specific exhibits.

fees_and_bonds: Unconfirmed; obtain current fee/bond/insurance schedule by road owner.
